notes.7: In this question, option C was incorrect (and therefore the key) because the momentum of the hot gas and the momentum of the rocket are in different directions. Momentum is a vector quantity and so, although the magnitudes of the two are equal, one is considered to be positive and the other negative.
notes.10: Most candidates showed a good understanding of the work done when different loads are move through different distances.
notes.11: Candidates showed a good understanding of evaporation, and this question was usually answered correctly. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0625 Physics November 2021
notes.18: Candidates needed to read the question carefully. The question asked which row in the table does not show a correct unit for the quantity in the left-hand column. The symbol λ does not represent a unit and is merely used to label an unknown wavelength.
notes.19: Only stronger candidates answered this correctly. Candidates needed to link the two formulae n = 1 / sin c and n = sin i / sin r. Although many candidates clearly attempted to do this, many forgot the inversion in the latter formula.
notes.21: A large majority of candidates were able to recognise the reversed image that is seen in a plane mirror.
notes.22: Although many candidates got this correct, there was a significant minority who did not recognise that it takes light from the Sun approximately 8 minutes to reach the Earth.
notes.26: The circuit symbol for the ammeter was correctly identified by most candidate.
notes.28: Only stronger candidates answered this correctly. The circuit is a form of potentiometer, the current is the same in both resistors and therefore (using V = I R ) the potential difference across the 2.0 Ω is twice that across the 1.0 Ω resistor. The total potential difference across the two resistors is the sum of the potential differences across the two resistors which is 18 V.
notes.31: A large majority of candidates recognised that the e.m.f. of the battery was the sum of the e.mf.s of the individual cells in series.
notes.37: This question was challenging for some candidates. They thought that the neutron number fell by 4. This may have been because candidates did not read the question carefully enough and were confused between neutron number and nucleon number.
notes.39: Only stronger candidates used the information about the half-life of the isotope that was given. If the term half-life was understood then candidates would have known that the count rate would have fallen to half the initial rate after six hours; after another six hours it would have fallen to half again, i.e., a quarter of the initial count. Graph C should have been identifiable as the only possible graph. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0625 Physics November 2021
